title: Drill #1501: Students Full Metric Union Stack
scenario: Management wants an un-deduplicated stack of high-metric and low-metric Students combined into a single unified stream.
businessObjective: Combine two query result sets from Students using UNION ALL to stack rows without deduplication.
schemaSnippet: id, name, major, gpa, year_level, enrollment_date
targetQuery: SELECT name AS name, gpa AS metric FROM Students WHERE gpa > 50 UNION ALL SELECT name AS name, gpa AS metric FROM Students WHERE gpa <= 50;
syntaxRule: UNION ALL directly appends result sets from two SELECT statements. It does NOT remove duplicate rows and avoids the sorting overhead of UNION.
syntaxTrap: Both SELECT queries must have the exact same number of columns with compatible data types.
eli5Story: Think of UNION ALL as taping two lists together end-to-end. It takes every single row from list 1 and dumps list 2 right under it without checking for duplicates.
commonMistakes: Using UNION instead of UNION ALL when duplicates should be preserved or sorting is unnecessary
Mismatched column counts between the top and bottom queries
learningOutcomes: Master basic row concatenation with UNION ALL
Understand performance advantages of avoiding implicit deduplication

title: Drill #1511: Students Distinct Attribute Union
scenario: The analytics department needs a distinct, unique roster of major values extracted from both high-value and early Students rows.
businessObjective: Combine two SELECT queries with UNION to automatically discard duplicate rows.
schemaSnippet: id, name, major, gpa, year_level, enrollment_date
targetQuery: SELECT major FROM Students WHERE gpa > 40 UNION SELECT major FROM Students WHERE id < 5;
syntaxRule: UNION performs an implicit DISTINCT across the combined result set, executing an internal sort or hash to eliminate identical rows.
syntaxTrap: UNION has a performance cost on large tables because the database must sort the combined rows to drop duplicates. Use UNION ALL if duplicates are impossible or acceptable.
eli5Story: UNION is like combining two guest lists and erasing anyone whose name appears on both lists, so each name only appears once.
commonMistakes: Forgetting that UNION discards duplicate values across both sets
Assuming UNION runs faster than UNION ALL
learningOutcomes: Use UNION for set union with automatic deduplication
Evaluate sort overhead vs row uniqueness requirements

title: Drill #1521: Students Strict Two-Column Arity Match
scenario: Ensure the set query adheres strictly to relational calculus by matching identical column arity (2 columns) across both branches.
businessObjective: Construct a set query ensuring column count and data types are aligned.
schemaSnippet: id, name, major, gpa, year_level, enrollment_date
targetQuery: SELECT id AS entity_id, name AS entity_label FROM Students WHERE id <= 5 UNION ALL SELECT id AS entity_id, name AS entity_label FROM Students WHERE id > 5;
syntaxRule: Set operators require identical column arity (the same number of selected attributes) in every branch of the query.
syntaxTrap: Attempting to SELECT 3 columns in the top query and 2 columns in the bottom query causes a fatal SQL syntax error.
eli5Story: You cannot stack a 2-column table on top of a 3-column table—the blocks won't fit! Every query in the union must have the exact same number of columns.
commonMistakes: Selecting different numbers of columns across UNION branches
Mismatching data types (e.g., stacking text onto integers without casting)
learningOutcomes: Enforce strict column count parity across set operations
Guarantee type compatibility between corresponding columns

title: Drill #1551: Students Disjoint Partition Segmentation
scenario: Split Students into distinct operational segments (Group A and Group B) using two targeted SELECT queries united together.
businessObjective: Use UNION ALL to combine mutually exclusive subsets of the same table with clear segment labels.
schemaSnippet: id, name, major, gpa, year_level, enrollment_date
targetQuery: SELECT name, 'Students Group A' AS partition_segment FROM Students WHERE id <= 3 UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Students Group B' AS partition_segment FROM Students WHERE id >= 8;
syntaxRule: When queries target non-overlapping (disjoint) conditions on the same table, UNION ALL is faster than UNION because deduplication is logically unnecessary.
syntaxTrap: Using UNION instead of UNION ALL on mutually exclusive subsets wastes CPU cycles on deduplication scans.
eli5Story: If you already know the two baskets have completely different items, don't waste time checking for duplicates—just dump them together with UNION ALL!
commonMistakes: Defaulting to UNION when sets are already guaranteed to be disjoint
Forgetting the segment label literal
learningOutcomes: Partition data streams using disjoint queries
Optimize performance by selecting UNION ALL for known non-overlapping sets

scenario: Construct a 3-way UNION ALL pipeline categorizing Students into High, Mid, and Low tiers, sorted alphabetically by entity name.

UNION ALL

UNION ALL

ORDER BY col ASC;
syntaxRule: You can chain arbitrarily many SELECT queries with UNION / UNION ALL. The trailing ORDER BY sorts the aggregated outcome of all combined branches.
